Article Title: 'I was really angry': Ex-India cricketer fumes over Rohit Sharma retirement saga
Article Text:
India's Rohit Sharma (ANI Photo)

Former India wicketkeeper Deep Dasgupta has criticised the speculation surrounding Rohit Sharma 's future during India's ODI series against England, saying the retirement rumours should never have gained traction while the team was still competing.The debate erupted after Rohit's early dismissal in the second ODI at Cardiff, with reports claiming the veteran opener would retire from ODIs after the series finale at Lord's. The report also suggested that the Indian team management was prepared to move on from the former captain because of his inconsistent form.The rumours gathered enough momentum for the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) to step in, with secretary Devajit Saikia dismissing the claims as baseless.Rohit responded in the best possible manner on the field. The opener smashed 138 off 110 balls in the third ODI at Lord's, although India eventually fell 27 runs short while chasing 388 and lost the three-match series 2-1.Reflecting on the episode, Dasgupta admitted he was frustrated by the discussions that dominated the series and questioned why such conversations had surfaced in the first place."I want to vent my anger a bit here because I was really angry when I was reading and listening to all of this.It is simple that as long as you keep scoring runs, you will keep playing. The only question comes in when that environment is created. Honestly, I have not heard it from any selector, captain, or the coach. It is a different matter if it was said off the field, which I am not privy to," he said on his YouTube channel.Following the conclusion of the series, Rohit also addressed the speculation in a video released by the BCCI, insisting that outside noise would not distract him from his responsibilities."What really matters is what I do on the field, try and contribute to the success of the team. That's where all my focus is. Let the noise be there, if there is no noise there is no fun. My job is inside, their job is outside, that's how I look at it," he said.India's next ODI assignment is a home series against the West Indies in September.Dasgupta also urged the selectors and team management to avoid creating unnecessary uncertainty around senior players such as Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli as India build towards the 2027 ODI World Cup.According to the former wicketkeeper, selection should continue to be based on performances rather than treating established stars differently."When you know that performances are needed, then these type of talks should not happen at all. Some people might get more chances, like Virat, Rohit, Shubman, they have been doing really well for years. It is not a debate about Rohit, it is a debate about everyone. When there are so many matches, it will happen, so just leave them alone. Don't treat them separately. Nothing has to change, just keep it simple," he concluded.
Article Summary: Former India wicketkeeper criticises speculation surrounding Rohit Sharma's future. Reports claimed Sharma would retire from ODI cricket after series against England. Dasgupta says rumours should never have gained traction while India were still competing. India lost the three-match series 2-1.

Article Title: 'It means the world': Anahat Singh's first reaction after winning World Junior Squash Championship
Article Text:
Sourav Ghosal and Anahat Singh (Image credit: X)

'A historic moment for Indian squash '



NEW DELHI: India No. 1 Anahat Singh on Saturday created history by becoming the first Indian to win the World Junior Squash Championship. The 18-year-old defeated Egypt's Ruqayya Salem 11-3, 11-7, 11-9 in the women's final in Ontario on Saturday."It means the world. I still feel like I’m dreaming," Anahat said after her title win."I’ve been losing in the semis and quarters over the last four years. I’ve always said, if anyone’s asked, ‘This tournament’s a curse,’ and I’ve never been able to play well in the event," the Delhi player said.Anahat said winning the title in her final junior appearance made the achievement even more special."This is my last year (as a junior) and my only chance to win it.It means the world," Anahat added.She also revealed that her focus before the final was to stay relaxed and enjoy the occasion."I knew if I’m stressed, I play terribly, so I just came out on court and hit my lines well… I wanted to enjoy every moment of getting to play in a world championship final," she said.Squash Rackets Federation of India (SRFI) secretary-general Cyrus Poncha described Anahat's victory as a milestone for the sport in the country."It’s a historic moment for Indian squash. Anahat has the potential to reach great heights," Poncha said.He also recalled the vision of late SRFI patron N. Ramachandran."(The late) Mr N Ramachandran, SRFI patron and visionary of Indian Squash Academy, always said it was his dream that India produce a world champion in individual events," Poncha continued."We achieved it in doubles, but to replicate that success in singles, it is really a dream come true. A lot of hard work and effort by Anahat, of course, but we've had the entire nation behind her and her successes over the last few years."
Article Summary: India No. 1 Anahat Singh becomes first Indian to win World Junior Squash Championship. The 18-year-old defeated Egypt's Ruqayya Salem 11-3, 11-7,11-9 in the women's final in Ontario on Saturday.

Article Title: 'Why not?': Ashwin makes strong case for Bhuvneshwar Kumar's India comeback ahead of 2027 World Cup
Article Text:
Bhuvneshwar Kumar (ANI Photo)

Former India off-spinner R Ashwin has thrown his weight behind Bhuvneshwar Kumar 's return to the national setup, urging the selectors to consider the veteran fast bowler as India prepare for the 2027 ODI World Cup.Ashwin believes India's current pace attack lacks the experience required for a major ICC tournament and pointed to Bhuvneshwar's recent success with Royal Challengers Bengaluru in the Indian Premier League as evidence that the 36-year-old still has plenty to offer.Bhuvneshwar played a key role in RCB's back-to-back IPL title-winning campaigns, claiming 45 wickets across the last two seasons. His consistent performances helped the franchise end its long wait for a trophy before successfully defending the title.Speaking on his YouTube channel, Ashwin argued that Bhuvneshwar deserves to be in contention for a World Cup berth, especially given his fitness and ability to contribute in multiple phases of the game."Why not? The way our fast bowling stocks are right now, there is some struggle there. I think it is worth considering Bhuvneshwar Kumar. Why can you not consider him? There is only one difference between Shami and Bhuvneshwar.Bhuvi has been able to put himself on the park for two seasons together for RCB and has been able to keep himself fit. Both teams RCB won the title, and he was also among the top three reasons for that. He looks fit enough. I am not saying to take him straightaway, but at least give him a chance and then decide. He can swing the ball, give you overs at the death and bat a bit as well. He has a lot of batting ability," said Ashwin.The former spinner also questioned whether India's relatively inexperienced fast-bowling unit would be ready for the pressures of a World Cup campaign. While acknowledging the promise shown by the younger pacers, he felt a blend of youth and experience would be a more balanced approach."Just because of the pure inexperience of the bowling attack, you can keep him in consideration. Gurnoor, Prasidh, and Prince - is that the bowling you want to play in a World Cup? I am not too sure. You can have one or two from these. Apart from that, you have Harshit and Bumrah. So with Bhuvneshwar, experience and youth will work well," he added.Ashwin further stressed that India should now focus on settling their pace attack rather than continuing to experiment, with the World Cup only a year away.According to him, the selectors have already handed opportunities to several fast bowlers and should now narrow down the core group while keeping Bhuvneshwar firmly in the conversation."It is not the time to develop players now with 12 months to go. You gave Harshit an opportunity, and it is important to know his status now as he bats at eight. Gurnoor and Prasidh got opportunities. But you cannot remove them and bring more bowlers now. It is important to identify who your four or five pacers are, out of which you will take three for the World Cup. That is why you must have someone like Bhuvneshwar Kumar in discussions as well," he explained.
Article Summary: Bhuvneshwar Kumar played a key role in RCB's back-to-back IPL title-winning campaigns. R Ashwin believes India's current pace attack lacks the experience required for a major ICC tournament. The former spinner also questioned whether India's relatively inexperienced fast-bowling unit would be ready for the pressures of a World Cup campaign.

Article Title: World Cup gold-medallist rower fails dope test
Article Text: PUNE: In a major embarrassment for Indian rowing, and the Army Rowing Node (ARN) in particular, World Cup gold medallist Lakshay has been provisionally suspended after testing positive in an out-of-competition dope test.Lakshay, who combined with Ujjwal Singh to win the lightweight double sculls gold at World Cup III in Switzerland last month, tested positive for stanozolol in a sample collected in Pune on May 25.The triumph was India’s first-ever gold at a rowing World Cup. The result now stands to be annulled if the anti-doping violation is confirmed. The development is also a blow to India’s preparations for this year’s Asian Games, with the Lakshay-Ujjwal combination considered a medal prospect.The 23-year-old havildar from Haryana had won the lightweight double sculls gold with Ajay Tyagi at last year’s Asian Championships in Vietnam, where he was also part of the silver-winning quadruple sculls team.
Article Summary: Lakshay tested positive for stanozolol in an out-of-competition dope test. Lakshay combined with Ujjwal Singh to win the lightweight double sculls gold at World Cup III in Switzerland. The triumph was India’s first-ever gold at a rowing World Cup.

Article Title: Abhishek Sharma scripts history, enters Indian cricket's record books
Article Text:
India's Abhishek Sharma (AP Photo)

Tests: Vinoo Mankad – 8/52 vs Pakistan (1952)

ODIs: Ravi Shastri – 5/15 vs Australia (1991)

T20Is: Abhishek Sharma – 3/17 vs Zimbabwe (2026)

India all-rounder Abhishek Sharma etched his name into the record books after registering the best bowling figures by an Indian opener in T20I cricket during the second T20I against Zimbabwe on Saturday.The left-arm spinner returned figures of 3/17, surpassing every Indian opener to produce the finest bowling performance in the shortest format. His spell came as India thrashed Zimbabwe by 90 runs to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series. Abhishek 's effort now sits alongside two iconic performances by Indian openers across formats. Vinoo Mankad continues to hold the record in Tests with his remarkable 8/52 against Pakistan in 1952, while Ravi Shastri's 5/15 against Australia in 1991 remains the best by an Indian opener in ODIs.Best bowling figures by an Indian opener:Abhishek had endured a disappointing outing with the bat after being dismissed cheaply by Blessing Muzarabani, but he made a decisive impact with the ball. Introduced as a part-time option, the left-arm spinner struck three times to ensure Zimbabwe never recovered during their daunting chase of 220.Zimbabwe's pursuit lost momentum after Brian Bennett's early aggression was cut short, and the visitors kept chipping away at regular intervals.Abhishek's three wickets, along with two each from Yash Thakur and Prince Yadav, bundled the hosts out for 129.Earlier, India recovered from 29/2 thanks to Ishan Kishan 's commanding 81 and Tilak Varma's unbeaten 60. Kishan steadied the innings before accelerating in the latter half of his knock, while Tilak produced a fluent half-century to power India to 219/5.The bowlers then completed the job in emphatic fashion, with Abhishek capping off the victory by creating a new Indian record.
Article Summary: Abhishek Sharma takes best bowling figures by an Indian opener in T20I cricket. Left-arm spinner takes 3/17 as India thrash Zimbabwe by 90 runs. India take an unassailable 2-0 lead in three-match series.

Article Title: 'Gens Una Sumus' - What three Latin words beneath a chess emblem taught me about the world
Article Text:
(

Aarav Dengla

is India’s 93rd Grandmaster. He is a keen observer and student of the world history in general and chess history in particular)

My earliest memory of chess is from when I was seven years old.Walking into the venue of my first international tournament, my hand tucked inside my mother's, I stopped beneath the emblem of FIDE, the international federation governing chess. Three words, printed in a language I didn't understand, caught my eye.Gens Una Sumus.As I stood there trying to make sense of them, my mother gently squeezed my hand and reminded me that my game was about to begin.Afterwards, I found her waiting in a quiet corner of the dining area and asked what the words meant. She searched on her phone and told me they were Latin for: "We are one family."Since then, I have seen those words at tournaments across the world.Most players walk beneath them without noticing. I still do. They remind me that every time I enter a tournament hall, I am stepping into a community bound by shared values.Years later, I learned that the phrase predates modern chess by more than fifteen centuries. It comes from the Roman poet Claudian, whose words were later adopted by the chess world. Their meaning evolved - from describing one people to reminding us that, through chess, we become one family.That may sound like an ambitious motto for a sport. But after years of travelling to tournaments, I have come to believe it reflects the reality of chess.Chess is one of the few sports where almost anyone can compete on equal terms. You don't need expensive equipment or a particular physique. The board is the same in Reykjavik as it is in Chennai. Tournaments are held in grand hotels, school auditoriums and community halls, yet the rules never change. In most open events, anyone can enter.That means a child who learned the game only a few years earlier can be paired against someone who has spent decades playing it.I experienced that when I was eight years old in a town nestled in the Austrian Alps. My opponent was a man in his fifties. Our game lasted more than five hours and stretched well past midnight. The organisers waited patiently for us to finish because neither of us was willing to give up a square or agree to a draw.Across the board, age no longer mattered. Neither did reputation. There were only two players trying to solve the same position.Chess also brings people physically closer than most sports. We sit just across the board from each other for hours. We notice the slightest change in breathing, how long a hand hovers above a piece, the sudden stillness after a mistake, or the quiet confidence that follows a good move.Then the game ends. We shake hands. We reset the pieces.And more often than not, we sit down again - this time beside each other rather than opposite each other - to analyse what happened."I should have castled here.""No, I think the problem started earlier. Look at your knight."Only moments earlier, we were trying to outthink each other. Now we are trying to understand the game together.That has always fascinated me.Victory and defeat matter deeply while the clock is running. But once the clocks stop, curiosity usually takes over. Opponents become collaborators. Together, we search for the moment the game changed and help each other discover what we had both missed.Perhaps that is what Gens Una Sumus has come to mean to me.Chess does not erase differences. Tournament halls still contain rivalry, disappointment, ambition and, sometimes, genuine dislike. It is far from a perfect world.But it repeatedly places strangers across from one another and asks them to engage with respect. For a few hours, the person sitting opposite cannot be reduced to a nationality, an age, a rating or a stereotype. Every move demands that you take them seriously.When I first saw those three Latin words at the age of seven, I knew nothing about their history. I didn't know they had travelled across centuries before finding a home in the chess world.I only knew they made me stop.Today, after years of sitting across the board from people older and younger than me, from countries I had never visited and cultures I knew little about, I understand them differently.Every tournament begins with sixty-four squares.Many end with one more human connection.Gens Una Sumus.We are one family.
Article Summary: Chess is one of the few sports where almost anyone can compete on equal terms. The board is the same in Reykjavik as it is in Chennai. Tournaments are held in grand hotels, school auditoriums and community halls. In most open events, anyone can enter.

Article Title: 'Think about cricket, not social media': Ishan Kishan to Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
Article Text:
Ishan Kishan and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (AFP Photo)

NEW DELHI: India wicketkeeper-batter Ishan Kishan has backed teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, saying the 15-year-old has all the qualities to become a match-winner for the national team.Kishan'c comments came after India's 90-run win over Zimbabwe in the second T20I in Harare on Saturday. India were in early trouble after losing Abhishek Sharma (8) and Sooryavanshi (20) inside the first three overs, slipping to 29/2. Kishan then played a brilliant knock of 81 off 44 balls to guide India to 219/5. Zimbabwe were later bowled out for 129 as India sealed the three-match series 2-0 with one game to spare.Kishan said the senior members of the squad are helping Sooryavanshi settle into international cricket and are encouraging him to ignore distractions away from the game."Vaibhav is actually very smart. He knows what he is doing," Kishan said after India's win."He knows how he has to bat and how he has to carry himself on and off the field."The wicketkeeper-batter revealed that he, Abhishek Sharma, captain Axar Patel and other experienced players regularly speak to the youngster to ensure he remains focused."When you represent India, you have to know what to focus on," he said."Me, Abhishek, Axar bhai and many others keep telling him to think about cricket, not social media or outside noise."Kishan said the team wants Sooryavanshi to learn from the experiences of the senior players and avoid getting distracted early in his career."When you have such a player and you know that he is very young, you will never want him to be distracted for the wrong reasons."So our job as a team, we are like brothers and he comes from my place, so we just have to be happy, focus on the important things. The mistakes we have made in our starting, he should not do that. He should enjoy his cricket, like he is doing now."Kishan believes Sooryavanshi's attacking style can have a major impact on India's performances."If he stays on the pitch, the difference he can create for the team is huge. A player who can attack from the first ball can take you to 80-90 runs in the powerplay," he said.
Article Summary: India wicketkeeper-batter Ishan Kishan has backed teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. The comments came after India's 90-run win over Zimbabwe in the second T20I in Harare. India sealed the three-match series 2-0 with one game to spare.

Article Title: The Hundred: New era, familiar result for London Spirit as Liam Livingstone heroics fall short
Article Text:
London Spirit captain Liam Livingstone scored a 40-ball 69 against Manchester Giants (ECB)

TimesofIndia.com in London:

Poll Vote & Share your view What was the most entertaining moment of the match? Liam Livingstone's all-round performance The tense final over 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

New owners, new coaches, new players and a new captain. London Spirit arrived at Lord's on Thursday promising a fresh start, but their opening day of The Hundred 2026 produced a painfully familiar result.For the fifth time in six seasons, Spirit's men began their campaign with defeat as Manchester Super Giants edged a thriller by seven runs in front of 23,847 spectators. Earlier, Spirit's women had been comprehensively beaten by seven wickets, completing a double defeat for the hosts.In between came a distinctly Hundred-style interlude, with rapper Tinie Tempah performing amid jets of fire and even venturing into the Lord's crowd.But once attention returned to the cricket, it was Liam Livingstone who provided the evening's real entertainment.Spirit's new captain almost single-handedly dragged his side towards victory with an extraordinary all-round performance.Having put Manchester in, Spirit were initially made to toil by Tim Seifert, who marked his first Hundred appearance with 67 from 45 balls. The New Zealander added 49 with Jos Buttler (16) and 40 with Heinrich Klaasen (17) as the visitors reached 103 for two.That was when Livingstone took matters into his own hands.The captain bowled 20 of the final 25 deliveries, conceding only 14 runs and taking two wickets as Manchester spectacularly lost seven wickets for 35 runs. Six of those fell for just 22 runs in the final 26 balls, leaving the visitors on 138 for nine.On a Lord's surface where batters struggled for timing, only four days after England and India had combined for 747 runs in an ODI, Manchester's total appeared around par.Spirit's chase quickly ran into trouble when James Rew departed for a two-ball duck. Livingstone rebuilt alongside Kiran Carlson (19) before adding 68 with Dewald Brevis, although the South African's 22 came from 23 balls as the required rate climbed.With 56 needed from 30 balls, Livingstone shifted gears.He took 12 from Noor Ahmad's final five deliveries and brought up his half-century from 32 balls with a trademark slog sweep. Manchester also gave him a helping hand, most notably when Seifert spilled a chance at deep midwicket and watched the ball bounce over the boundary for six.Suddenly, Spirit were back in it.They required 21 from the final 10 deliveries, but Manchester's England pace duo held their nerve. Gus Atkinson removed Brevis with a caught-and-bowled dismissal and finished with figures of two for 15, leaving Sonny Baker to defend 12 from the final five balls.Baker had conceded 25 runs from his first 15 deliveries, while Livingstone had already struck five sixes.This time, however, the 23-year-old seamer won the battle. After conceding three runs from his first two deliveries, Baker went full and fast and crashed into Livingstone's stumps. James Coles was caught off the final ball as Spirit finished on 131 for six.Livingstone's 69 from 40 balls, coupled with figures of two for 14, earned him the Match Hero award but not the result."We bowled some really good stuff through the middle, dragged it back towards the end, and we nearly chased it down," Livingstone said. "We just got a bit too far behind the rate to catch up in the end."There was considerably less drama in the women's game.Grace Harris struck the opening delivery for four, but Spirit promptly collapsed to 23 for four in the powerplay and were eventually bowled out for 80 in 91 balls.Manchester needed only 59 deliveries to complete a seven-wicket win, with Paige Scholfield finishing the chase with successive four and six.For London Spirit, it was a sobering beginning to what was supposed to be a fresh chapter. Livingstone believes there is something to build on, and his own performance certainly provided encouragement.But for all the changes around Lord's, opening night brought the same old outcome: two games, two defeats.
Article Summary: Liam Livingstone scored a 40-ball 69 against Manchester Giants. Spirit's women were beaten by seven wickets by Manchester Super Giants. Tinie Tempah performed amid jets of fire and even venturing into the Lord's crowd. For the fifth time in six seasons, Spirit's men began their campaign with defeat.

Article Title: Chess legend Viswanathan Anand steps in as FIDE interim president after EU sanctions sideline Arkady Dvorkovich
Article Text:
Arkady Dvorkovich (on left) and Viswanathan Anand (PTI Photo)

AICF welcomes Anand's new role

India's Chess Olympiad squads announced

NEW DELHI: International Chess Federation (FIDE) President Arkady Dvorkovich has stepped aside from his role after being included in the European Union's latest sanctions list linked to Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine. The decision means FIDE Deputy President and former world champion Viswanathan Anand will serve as the interim president until the sanctions are lifted or overturned.In a statement released by FIDE, Dvorkovich described the sanctions as unjust and confirmed that he would challenge them through legal channels. However, he said his decision to temporarily suspend himself was taken to ensure the smooth functioning of the global governing body."Today, the EU decision to include my name in the 21st sanctions list was published. I want to state unequivocally that I consider this decision unlawful and unfair, and this decision will be immediately challenged by all possible means. I am confident that justice will prevail," FIDE's statement reads.He added that remaining in office while under sanctions could affect FIDE's day-to-day operations."However, given that until a formal court decision is rendered and/or such decision is cancelled or amended, these sanctions could hinder the stable functioning of FIDE, I have decided to voluntarily suspend the exercise of my powers and duties as FIDE President with immediate effect and for as long as I remain subject to sanctions under the EU and Swiss laws and regulations."Under Article 19.2 of the FIDE Charter, Anand will now take over as Interim President.The FIDE Council formally accepted Dvorkovich's decision and confirmed that he would not exercise any presidential powers or control over the federation or its assets while the sanctions remain in force.The FIDE presidential election at the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand will go ahead as scheduled.The move was welcomed by All India Chess Federation (AICF) President Nitin Narang, who expressed confidence in Anand's leadership."As FIDE enters an interim phase of leadership, I extend my best wishes to Deputy President Viswanathan Anand as he assumes the responsibilities of Interim President," he wrote on X."Vishy sir has earned the respect of the global chess community through his integrity, wisdom and lifelong service to our sport. I am confident that under his stewardship, FIDE will continue to uphold stability, good governance and its commitment to players and federations across the world."The EU's 21st sanctions package targets 170 entities and 48 individuals with measures including possible asset freezes and travel bans. Despite the leadership change, FIDE said its activities, tournaments and social programmes will continue without interruption.Meanwhile, India has also announced its squads for the FIDE Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, to be held from September 17 to 27.Defending champions India will be led by reigning world champion D Gukesh, alongside R Praggnanandhaa, Arjun Erigaisi, Nihal Sarin and Vidit Gujrathi in the open section, while Koneru Humpy headlines the women's team with R Vaishali, Divya Deshmukh, Vantika Agrawal and Savitha Shri B.
Article Summary: International Chess Federation (FIDE) President Arkady Dvorkovich has stepped aside from his role after being included in the European Union's latest sanctions list linked to Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine. FIDE Deputy President and former world champion Viswanathan Anand will serve as the interim president until the sanctions are lifted or overturned.

Article Title: India at CWG 2026: Know Your Athlete - Minakshi Harichandra Jadhav (Wheelchair Basketball, 3x3)
Article Text:
Minakshi Harichandra Jadhav

Event: Women's 3x3 Wheelchair BasketballCWG Record: Team captain of India's debut squad in the event — the country's first-ever team sport qualification in Para competition at the Commonwealth Games.Major Achievements:2025 IWBF Asia-Oceania Championships (Bangkok): Led India to qualification for the Commonwealth Games for the first time in this eventSelected as captain of India's four-member squad for Glasgow 2026Minakshi Jadhav, from Satara district in Maharashtra, sustained a spinal cord injury in a fall from a tree in 2012, at age 23. Article Title: Asian Games 2026 Cricket Schedule: India, Pakistan on opposite sides of draw - full fixtures revealed
Article Text:
India's Richa Ghosh bats during the ICC Women's T20 World Cup, Group 1 cricket match between India and Pakistan in Birmingham, England. (Photo by AP/PTI)

Women's team to begin against Japan

The schedule for the cricket events at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, has been announced, with defending champions India receiving direct entry into the quarter-finals in both the men's and women's T20 tournaments.Cricket will be played in the T20 format and will have full international status. The women's competition will run from September 17 to 22, while the men's tournament will take place from September 24 to October 1 at Korogi Athletic Park in Aichi Prefecture.India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh have all been seeded into the men's quarter-finals based on their rankings. The remaining four quarter-final spots will be decided through a preliminary stage featuring six teams split into two groups.Group A includes Afghanistan, Japan and Nepal, while Group B features Hong Kong China, Malaysia and Oman.The top two teams from each group will qualify for the quarter-finals. Since India and Pakistan are on opposite sides of the draw, the two rivals can only meet if both reach the semi-finals or the final.India will face one of the teams that qualify from the preliminary round in the quarter-finals.India's women's team will start its title defence against hosts Japan in the quarter-finals. If India win, they will face either Bangladesh or China in the semi-finals.The other quarter-final matches will see Sri Lanka take on Malaysia, while Pakistan will play Thailand. India will be aiming to retain the gold medals won in both the men's and women's competitions at the Hangzhou Asian Games in 2023.
Article Summary: The schedule for the cricket events at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, has been announced. Defending champions India receive direct entry into the quarter-finals in both the men's and women's T20 tournaments. The women's competition will run from September 17 to 22. The men's tournament will take place from September 24 to October 1.

Article Title: From doubt to dominance: Jadumani Singh's career-changing move to 55kg fuels CWG dream
Article Text:
Jadumani Singh Mandengbam from India in red (Photo by Getty Images)

When Jadumani Singh decided to move up from 50kg to the 55kg category, there were plenty of doubters. Many believed the Manipuri boxer, shorter than most of his rivals in the division, would struggle against bigger opponents.Some even warned that the move could derail the momentum he had built after capping an impressive 2025 season with a silver medal at the World Boxing Cup Finals in the men's 50kg.The 23-year-old from Iroishemba in Manipur, however, chose to block out the noise.Months later, the gamble paid off. Jadumani not only won the national title in his new weight class and was adjudged the Best Boxer of the tournament, but also secured place in India’s squads for the Commonwealth Games and the Asian Games “People kept saying I wouldn’t be able to do well in 55kg because of my height. At times, it affected me mentally, but deep down I believed I could succeed,” said Jadumani, who will begin his CWG campaign against Scotland’s Aaron Cullen in the men’s 55kg Round of 32 on Friday.The move was driven by a bigger ambition. With the 51kg category no longer part of Los Angeles Olympics programme and his long-term target being an Olympic medal, Jadumani realised he had to think beyond immediate success.Before taking the plunge, he spent hours discussing the decision with former world champion L. Sarita Devi , who has remained one of his biggest mentors even after he joined the Army Sports Institute (ASI) in Pune.“That decision to move to 55kg became the biggest turning point of his career. Self-belief is the most important thing. I first asked him if he truly believed he could succeed in the new category. When he said yes, I told him I would support him completely,” Sarita said.The transition was anything but easy. Every bout at the National Championships tested him. Jadumani defeated several established names, including former Commonwealth Games champion Amit Panghal , before clinching the title and the Best Boxer award.“I didn’t pay attention to what anyone was saying. I just focused on my boxing. My only aim was to become champion,” he said.The national title proved to be the launchpad for an impressive run. Jadumani claimed bronze at Boxam Elite International in Spain, pushed top seed Rui Yamaguchi in a closely fought contest at the Asian Championships before bouncing back with gold at Grand Prix Usti Nad Labem in Czechia. He then topped the national trials to seal his place in India’s squads for the CWG and Asiad.The self-belief that carried him through the toughest phase of his career has been with him since he first stepped into a boxing ring. Introduced to the sport by his uncle, Mandengbam Milan Singh, Jadumani initially knew little about boxing.“My uncle wanted me to take up an individual sport. Everyone in the family played football, but he felt I would have a better future in boxing,” he said.Sarita’s influence, meanwhile, has extended far beyond technical guidance.“She has taught me discipline and the importance of maintaining my diet. Before every major competition, we speak over a video call. Whenever I feel low, she motivates me and helps me stay focused,” he said.As he prepares to make his Commonwealth Games debut in Glasgow, Jadumani believes the sacrifices have all been worthwhile. Last year, he managed to spend barely 15 to 20 days at home as he trained relentlessly to establish himself in the new weight category.Sarita believes the sacrifices will eventually bear fruit.“An athlete only needs one opportunity. Jadumani got that opportunity, proved himself, and I believe he has what it takes to win medals for India on the biggest stage,” she said with pride before signing off.
Article Summary: Jadumani Singh will make his Commonwealth Games debut on Friday. The 23-year-old moved up from 50kg to the 55kg category last year. He won the national title in his new weight class and was adjudged the Best Boxer of the tournament.

Article Title: Durand Cup set to introduce women's tournament from next edition
Article Text:
Durand Cup Trophy tour concludes in Kolkata ahead of tournament opener (ANI Photo)

Kolkata: The oldest football tournament in Asia — Durand Cup — will host its 135th edition when Mohun Bagan Super Giant and East Bengal FC take the field at Salt Lake Stadium in the first derby of the season on Saturday.However, in the 134 years of the tournament’s existence, Indian women’s football has grown by leaps and bounds, and at the culmination of Durand Cup Trophy Tour in the city on Wednesday, the organisers of the prestigious competition — the Indian Armed Forces — revealed their enthusiasm to include a women’s competition in the coming years.At the ceremonial function and news conference at AOI Vijay Durg, where the tournament’s three iconic trophies were showcased, Major General Dinesh Kumar Singh, vice-chairman of Durand Cup Organising Committee, said they were mulling the introduction of a women’s tournament alongside the men’s event in the near future."Why leave the girls behind?" was the question on their minds six months ago when they began preparations for the upcoming season, Singh said.“So, this is something that we have already thought about. The issue is how many venues and what kind of facilities (will be available) for it. So probably in the next edition we may have a truncated or a smaller version of the girls’ event,” he added.To add to the expectations, a special women's exhibition match was organised jointly by the Indian Armed Forces and the govt of Manipur at the SAI Ground in Takyel, Imphal, in the build-up to the main competition.This time, the tournament will see 24 men’s teams compete across five venues, with Ranchi as the newest addition and the Assam matches returning to Guwahati after two editions in Kokrajhar.“We saw the enthusiasm among the people in Kokrajhar. But the state government wanted it back in Guwahati for ease of organisation,” said Lieutenant General Gambhir Singh, Chief of Staff, Headquarters Eastern Command, and chairman of the Organising Committee.Among the dignitaries at the event was chief guest Dr Indranil Khan, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for the Departments of Youth Services and Sports and Consumer Affairs in the West Bengal government.“During the recent FIFA World Cup , we all supported clubs from around the world. Now it is time to unite behind Indian football and our own footballers,” said Khan.Meanwhile, Ranchi will host its first-ever Durand Cup match on Sunday, when Jamshedpur FC take on Defenders FC at Birsa Munda Stadium. Defending champions NorthEast United FC will begin their title defence against Bodoland FC at Guwahati’s Indira Gandhi Athletic Stadium on Aug 1. The other cities hosting the premier competition are the football-crazy northeastern cities of Shillong and Imphal.
Article Summary: Mohun Bagan Super Giant and East Bengal FC take the field at Salt Lake Stadium on Saturday. Ranchi will host its first-ever Durand Cup match on Sunday, when Jamshedpur FC take on Defenders FC at Birsa Munda Stadium. Defending champions NorthEast United FC will begin their title defence against Bodoland FC at Guwahati’s Indira Gandhi Athletic Stadium on Aug 1.

Article Title: CWG 2026: Indian boxers unfazed by baggage snag on arrival
Article Text:
Santiago Nieva (Image credit: X)

India’s boxing contingent arrived in Glasgow confident after a productive two-week multinational training camp in Belfast, but its final preparations were briefly disrupted when some boxers’ luggage failed to arrive ahead of Thursday’s opening ceremony.The 14-member squad travelled from Belfast to Glasgow on Tuesday after completing the intensive camp, during which the boxers benefitted from quality sparring and competition-specific training. However, several athletes were left without their bags, which also contained their ceremonial outfits, TOI has learnt.Sources said officials from the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and the chef-de-mission’s office were at the airport on Wednesday, coordinating with the airline to ensure the baggage reached the contingent before the ceremony. The boxing competition begins on Friday and runs until Aug 1.The incident, however, has not gone down well with the Boxing Federation of India (BFI). Sources said that after the issue surfaced, the federation asked the boxers to submit declarations stating that they would not speak to the media about internal team matters and would instead remain focused on their performances.Despite the logistical hiccup, the mood in the camp remains upbeat. “We are settling in well in Glasgow. We had a good camp in Belfast where everybody got quality sparring and proper preparations. The boxers are managing their weights well. We will have the draws soon. We are coming with high expectations for this competition,” India women’s head coach Santiago Nieva told TOI .India’s 14-member squad features Olympic bronze medallist Lovlina Borgohain and Jaismine Lamboria, the world No. 1 in the women’s 57kg category.

Article Title: 'Not up to the standard': Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza blames pitch for India defeat
Article Text:
Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza on the right (ANI Photo)

Positives despite the defeat

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think the Zimbabwe team can bounce back in the series? Yes, they have the potential. No, India has the upper hand. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza blamed the pitch after his team's seven-wicket loss to India in the opening T20I of the three-match series at the Harare Sports Club.Raza said the surface had too much moisture early on, making batting difficult with the new ball, while conditions became much easier when India came out to chase. India comfortably chased 126 in 13.2 overs, powered by Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's record-breaking 18-ball half-century to take a 1-0 lead in the series.Raza felt the pitch favoured the team batting second and said Zimbabwe struggled because the ball continued to move for longer than expected."Again, not up to the standard, I think. In the morning, I think that moisture certainly played a part, but I didn't think it was going to play a part for that long.I thought it remained tough with the new ball," Raza said after the match."Unfortunately, we didn't hit many boundaries up front as well, so the ball stayed new, and because of that, I felt the movement off the deck made batting even tougher," he added.Comparing it with the recent Bangladesh ODI series, Raza said the wicket became much better to bat on during India's innings."I thought during the Bangladesh ODI series, there was a lot of moisture, and it remained there for a long time.Whereas today, I thought the moisture was there for the first eight to ten or even 12 overs, and apart from that, when India came out to bat, the wicket was very true," he said.Zimbabwe recovered from 32/4 to post 125/7, thanks to Wessly Madhevere and Tadiwanashe Marumani. Raza praised the pair for helping the team reach a respectable total and hoped the rest of the batting unit would contribute more in the coming matches."So, hopefully, we get a better wicket for the next game so that even when we lose the toss, it doesn't play too big a part," he added."Yes, definitely. That's one of the positives. Marumani and Madhevere, it's a new role as well. I thought they batted really well to give us some sort of a respectable total. We'll take that as a positive, and hopefully the other guys can chip in as well so that we can put up a competitive total if we bat first," he said.
Article Summary: Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza blamed the pitch after his team's seven-wicket loss to India in the opening T20I of the three-match series. Raza said the surface had too much moisture early on, making batting difficult with the new ball. India comfortably chased 126 in 13.2 overs to take a 1-0 lead in the series.

Article Title: Injuries denied her twice: Sakshi Chaudhary is finally ready for the Commonwealth Games
Article Text:
India's Sakshi Chaudhary (PTI Photo)

New Delhi :

In Haryana’s boxing heartland of Bhiwani, dreams are often forged inside crowded rings filled with aspiring boxers before blossoming on the world stage. Sakshi Chaudhary , a product of the famed Bhiwani Boxing Club, has travelled that familiar road, but not without heartbreak. Shoulder injuries robbed the 25-year-old of a place at the 2022 Birmingham Commonwealth Games and the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Games . Four years later, she finally gets her chance.When India’s boxing campaign begins at the Glasgow CWG, Sakshi will enter the ring as one of the country’s leading medal prospects. The women’s 51kg boxer opens her campaign against Botswana’s Lethabo Modukanele on July 27, carrying not just the nation’s hopes but also the weight of opportunities once lost.“The India jersey always motivates me to fight for gold. I had been waiting for this opportunity. After missing the CWG and Asian Games earlier because of injuries, I’m finally here.My preparations have been very good. I’ve sharpened my technique and attacking game, and my height and reach will be an advantage,” Sakshi told TOI .The boxer from Dhanana village, whose father is a farmer and mother a homemaker, credits legendary coach Jagdish Singh with shaping her career before she joined the Army. Her road to Glasgow required reinvention. A natural 54kg boxer, Sakshi dropped down to 51kg after Preeti Pawar secured India’s 54kg berth by winning gold at the Asian Championships.She shed nearly three kilograms in three weeks and justified the gamble, defeating Jyoti Gulia, former world champion Nikhat Zareen and reigning world champion Minakshi Hooda during the selection trials at NIS Patiala in May.“This was a do-or-die situation for me. I wanted to go all out because qualifying for the CWG and Asian Games meant everything after losing out previously,” she said.The move has also suited her boxing. “In 54kg, many boxers come down from higher weights and there’s more power. In 51kg, my height advantage helps me much more.”A two-time World youth champion, World junior champion and Asian Championships medallist, Sakshi is now making a smooth transition to senior boxing. For the boxer who once watched two major Games slip away, Glasgow offers the chance to script the comeback she has long imagined.Stay Updated With: CWG Schedule 2026
Article Summary: Sakshi Chaudhary is a product of the famed Bhiwani Boxing Club. The 25-year-old missed the 2022 Birmingham Commonwealth Games and the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Games due to injuries. Sakshi dropped to 51kg after Preeti Pawar secured India’s 54kg berth by winning gold at the Asian Championships.

Article Title: 'Where is Rajat Patidar?' - Former India batter questions selectors over Zimbabwe T20I squad
Article Text:
Rajat Patidar with the IPL trophy (ANI Photo)

Former India batter Hanuma Vihari has criticised the Indian team management for leaving Rajat Patidar out of India's T20I squad for the Zimbabwe series.Vihari believes Patidar deserved a place after his impressive performances and leadership with Royal Challengers Bengaluru, while also questioning the overall balance of the squad.India, however, made a strong start to the series by defeating Zimbabwe by seven wickets in the opening T20I at the Harare Sports Club on Thursday to take a 1-0 lead in the three-match contest.After restricting Zimbabwe to 125/7, India chased down the target in just 13.2 overs, thanks to a sensational half-century from 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who became the youngest player to score a fifty in men's international cricket.His 18-ball fifty included four fours and four sixes.Earlier, Mayank Yadav (2/18) and Prince Yadav (2/19) starred with the ball, while India also named role-specific concussion substitutes for the first time, including Suryansh Shedge, Prabhsimran Singh, Harsh Dubey and Yash Thakur.Vihari said the selectors made some difficult decisions, especially by leaving out Patidar despite the squad featuring several left-handed batters. He felt a right-handed batter like Patidar or Sanju Samson would have given the team better balance."Rinku Singh was brought back, but where is Rajat Patidar? He led RCB to titles in two seasons and also performed well as a batter. He was not considered as well. These are hard calls from the selectors. Patidar should have been given a chance, especially because if you look at the team, all are left-handers. With so many left-handers, Patidar or Samson as right-handers should have been there. Yes, Prabhsimran is there, but I don't think he will play because Ishan Kishan will be the first choice wicketkeeper," Vihari said on his YouTube channel.Vihari also questioned the omission of experienced wrist-spinner Kuldeep Yadav and wicketkeeper-batter Sanju Samson. He pointed out that Patidar scored 486 runs at a strike rate of 196.76 in IPL 2026 and felt performances should matter more than age while picking the squad."It's a serious case of why Kuldeep Yadav has not been included. He is a wrist-spinner with experience. Why did you not play him? Also, if you did not want Sanju Samson for the Zimbabwe series, you sent Prabhsimran. Fine. But you did not even consider giving an opportunity to Rajat Patidar. Why should age be a factor?" Vihari asked."If you have taken many players who performed in the IPL, then why not Patidar? You have filled the team with left-handers. There is no right-hander apart from Shreyas," he added.
Article Summary: Rajat Patidar left out of India's T20I squad for the Zimbabwe series. Former India batter Hanuma Vihari questions squad balance. India beat Zimbabwe by seven wickets to take 1-0 lead in the three-match series.

Article Title: 'What's his mistake?': Ex-India star wants India to make one big change for 3rd T20I vs Zimbabwe
Article Text:
BCCI Photo

NEW DELHI: Former India batter Aakash Chopra believes India should give Prabhsimran Singh a chance in the third and final T20I against Zimbabwe after already sealing the series. India have taken an unassailable 2-0 lead with convincing wins in the first two matches. The final game will be played in Harare on Sunday.Speaking on his YouTube channel, Chopra questioned why Prabhsimran has not been given an opportunity."I am thinking of playing Prabh (Prabhsimran Singh) as well. What's his mistake? You have selected Prabhsimran Singh, and we have no idea whatsoever when you would select him again.You have won the series," Chopra said.Chopra said India should continue backing Abhishek Sharma despite his poor scores in the first two matches. Instead, he suggested giving Ishan Kishan a break and bringing Prabhsimran into the playing XI. Abhished scored 1 run in the first T20I and then fell for 8 in the second T20I."So play him (Prabhsimran) in place of Abhishek, or else play him in place of Ishan. You can actually play him in place of Ishan.Don't play him in place of Abhishek. He hasn't scored runs. Two matches have gone badly for him. So play him the third as well. Make him score runs, and if a bowling option is required, make him do that job as well," the former opener said.Prabhsimran is yet to make his international debut. The Punjab Kings wicketkeeper-batter has scored 3,665 runs in 127 T20 innings at a strike rate of 151.50."Give a break to Ishan. Prabhsimran Singh will easily do the keeping job as well. So you can use him like that as a player. This is an opportunity that can be given to Prabh," he said.

Article Title: IND vs ZIM 2nd T20I: Ishan Kishan, Tilak Varma fire India to series win
Article Text:
BCCI Photo

Putting the bitter memories of their disastrous white-ball tour of Ireland and England behind them, India produced a dominant performance with bat and ball to clinch their first series win under new T20 captain Shreyas Iyer by crushing a hapless Zimbabwe by 90 runs in the second T20I at the Harare Sports Club on Saturday.India have taken an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series after following up their seven-wicket win in the opener with another emphatic victory. The last T20I of the series will be played today.After a disappointing tour of UK, the left-handed duo of wicketkeeperbatter Ishan Kishan (81 off 44 balls; 9x4, 2x6) and vice-captain Tilak Varma (60 not out off 29; 5x4, 3x6) smashed blistering half-centuries to propel India to 219/5. The visitors then bowled Zimbabwe out for 129 in 17.5 overs.Making an impressive T20I debut after replacing Ashok Sharma, Vidarbha’s Yash Thakur claimed 2-30. He snapped the key wicket of Zimbabwe’s top scorer Brian Bennett (32 off 19; 3x4, 3x6). Prince Yadav (2-10) continued his impressive series before limping off the field after bowling just 1.2 overs.Part-time left-arm spinner Abhishek Sharma (3-17) then cleaned up the tail to complete a dominant Indian performance.Asked to bat first, India lost their explosive opening pair of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (20 off 9; 3x4, 1x6) and Abhishek (8 off 8; 2x4) with only 29 on the board. Kishan then added 66 in 42 balls for the third wicket with skipper Shreyas Iyer (25 off 20; 4x4), before sharing a whirlwind 94-run stand in just 44 balls with Tilak for the fourth wicket to lift India to an imposing total.The pair came together at 95 for three in the 10th over after Iyer was caught at backward point by Brad Evans off Brian Bennett. They immediately shifted gears, plundering 77 runs in just 30 balls through the middle overs. From 111 for three in the 12th over, India surged to 188 for three by the end of the 17th, with the lefthanded pair taking apart the Zimbabwe attack, including 21 runs off the 15th over bowled by captain Sikandar Raza (0-47).India thus equalled their own record for the most 200-plus totals in a calendar year. This was their ninth T20I score of 200 or more in 2026, matching the mark they set in 2024.Brief scores: India 219/5 in 20 overs (I Kishan 81, T Varma 60 not out; B Muzarabani 1/36) beat Zimbabwe 129 all out in 17.5 overs (B Bennett 32; Y Thakur 2/30, P Yadav 2/10, A Sharma 3/17) by 90 runs.
Article Summary: India have taken an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series. Ishan Kishan (81) and Tilak Varma (60) smashed blistering half-centuries to propel India to 219/5. The visitors then bowled Zimbabwe out for 129 in 17.5 overs.

Article Title: Shreyas Iyer drops major selection hint after fresh India injury blow
Article Text:
India players celebrate (AP)

India captain Shreyas Iyer has indicated that the team management is likely to make changes to the playing XI for the third and final T20I against Zimbabwe after pacer Prince Yadav suffered a hamstring injury during the second match of the series.Having already secured the three-match contest with a 2-0 lead, India now have the freedom to rotate players ahead of Sunday's dead rubber.Prince's outing was cut short after the Delhi fast bowler pulled up midway through his run-up while bowling his second over. He immediately clutched his hamstring and walked off the field, ending what had been an impressive spell. Before leaving the field, the right-arm pacer had struck twice in just eight deliveries.Speaking after India's 90-run victory, Iyer admitted the injury could force the team into making changes."One of our players got injured unfortunately, so you might see a few changes tomorrow (Sunday)," Iyer said during the post-match presentation.Prince's setback adds to India's growing injury concerns over the past two months. The pacer himself had entered the squad as a replacement for Harshit Rana, who was ruled out after sustaining an injury during the T20I series against England.It remains unclear whether Prince will recover in time or require further assessment at the BCCI 's Centre of Excellence, as Rana did.Despite the injury concern, India have adequate cover in the pace department. Ashok Sharma, who made his T20I debut in the opening match of the series, is available as a like-for-like replacement if required.With the series already wrapped up, the final T20I also presents an opportunity for India to assess players who are yet to feature. Wicketkeeper-opener Prabhsimran Singh and spin-bowling all-rounder Harsh Dubey are among those waiting for a chance to make their T20I debuts.One possible change could involve resting Ishan Kishan , who has strengthened his place in the side after his match-winning 81 in the second T20I, and bringing in Prabhsimran. However, India have generally preferred to give players opportunities in their natural roles.Another option could be to rest opener Abhishek Sharma , who has not produced his best batting form in the series despite remaining India's first-choice opener. Such a move would allow Prabhsimran to slot into the top order without disrupting the team's preferred batting positions.With the series already decided, the third T20I offers India a chance to balance experimentation with the pursuit of a clean sweep over Zimbabwe.
Article Summary: Prince Yadav suffered a hamstring injury during the second match of the series. India captain Shreyas Iyer has indicated that the team management is likely to make changes to the playing XI for the third and final T20I against Zimbabwe. India have already secured the three-match contest with a 2-0 lead.

Article Title: WI vs PAK 1st Test: Kavem Hodge's unbeaten 83 helps West Indies reach 194/3 against Pakistan on rain-hit Day 1
Article Text:
Kavem Hodge (AFP Photo)

Pakistan strike early



Hodge survives review, reaches fifty



Abbas impresses with the ball



Chase chooses to bat first



Team changes for both sides



Tribute to Garfield Sobers



NEW DELHI: Kavem Hodge scored an unbeaten 83 to guide West Indies to 194/3 at stumps on a rain-affected opening day of the first Test against Pakistan at the Brian Lara Stadium in Trinidad on Saturday.Only 67 overs were possible on Day 1 as rain and bad light reduced play.Hodge stayed at the crease throughout the day and was joined by Shai Hope, who remained unbeaten on 39. The pair added an unbroken 88-run partnership for the fourth wicket to put West Indies in a strong position.Pakistan made an early breakthrough when fast bowler Mohammad Abbas dismissed Brandon King for 12 in the ninth over. West Indies were struggling at 13/1 as runs came slowly in the opening session.After lunch, the home side recovered with Hodge leading the fightback despite the pitch becoming more challenging after the rain. Tagenarine Chanderpaul scored 21 before falling to Aamer Jamal, who returned to Pakistan's Test side after an 18-month break. Amir Jangoo also made 21 before Abbas trapped him lbw.Hodge remained calm throughout his innings and completed his fourth Test half-century off 86 balls with eight fours.He also survived a big scare when Abbas struck him on the pads.The on-field umpire gave him out lbw, but Pakistan's decision was overturned after replays showed the ball was bouncing over the stumps.Hope gave him solid support, facing 91 deliveries before stumps.Abbas was Pakistan's best bowler, finishing the day with figures of 2/44 from 19 overs.Left-arm spinner Usman Ali made his Test debut at the age of 33 and showed promising signs by getting sharp turn from the surface.West Indies captain Roston Chase won the toss and decided to bat. The decision looked risky early as Pakistan's bowlers kept the scoring under control during the first session.The hosts, however, recovered well in the second and third sessions thanks to Hodge's patient innings.Pakistan are playing under the leadership of Babar Azam, who returned as captain after Shan Masood was removed from the role following 12 defeats in 16 Tests. Pakistan are also searching for their first away Test win since beating Sri Lanka in 2023.The visitors were without opener Abdullah Fazal, who was ruled out of this series and the upcoming England tour with a lower back injury. Imam-ul-Haq returned to partner Azan Awais at the top of the order.West Indies fielded three fast bowlers — Kemar Roach, Shamar Joseph and Jayden Seales — after Alzarri Joseph made himself unavailable for the series. Jomel Warrican is the team's specialist spinner.Both teams entered the series at the bottom of the World Test Championship standings with one win each.Before the start of play, players from both teams and the match officials observed a minute's silence in memory of West Indies legend Sir Garfield Sobers, who passed away earlier this month at the age of 89.West Indies players and match officials also wore black armbands as a mark of respect.
Article Summary: Kavem Hodge scored 83 to guide West Indies to 194/3 at stumps on the rain- affected opening day of the first Test against Pakistan. Only 67 overs were possible on Day 1 as rain and bad light reduced play. Hodge stayed at the crease throughout the day and was joined by Shai Hope who remained unbeaten on 39.

Article Title: 'My bad': Ishan Kishan's hilarious run-out blunder goes viral; India star laughs it off — WATCH
Article Text:
Ishan Kishan (Video grabs)

WATCH: Ishan Kishan's run out miss

Kishan laughs off viral moment

Brilliant 81 powers India to series-clinching win

NEW DELHI: Ishan Kishan was the undisputed star with the bat as India sealed the T20I series against Zimbabwe on Saturday, but it was a comical run-out miss behind the stumps that had social media buzzing long after the final ball.The wicketkeeper-batter, who smashed a brilliant 81 off 44 deliveries to earn the Player of the Match award, became the centre of attention for an amusing fielding lapse during Zimbabwe's chase. Kishan later saw the funny side of the incident, joking about it during the post-match presentation.The viral moment came in the 15th over when Zimbabwe's Tadiwanashe Marumani nudged the ball towards deep backward point.A mix-up between the batters left both stranded near the bowler's end, presenting India with what appeared to be a straightforward run-out opportunity.However, Kishan casually underarmed the throw towards the stumps, seemingly believing the batter had already made his ground. The throw neither hit the stumps nor reached Ravi Bishnoi for a backup attempt, allowing Zimbabwe to escape.Realising what had happened, Kishan immediately placed his hand on his head with a sheepish grin as teammates and fans were left in disbelief.The light-hearted moment quickly made the rounds on social media, and Kishan was asked about it after receiving the Player of the Match award."I thought the batter was already inside the crease, but my bad. I'll be looking at the bails next time," he said with a smile.Fortunately for India, the missed chance had no bearing on the outcome as Zimbabwe were eventually bundled out for 129, handing the visitors a commanding 90-run victory and an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series.Kishan ensured his amusing run-out miss remained only a footnote by producing a superb innings after India slipped to 29/2 inside the powerplay.The left-hander first rebuilt the innings with captain Shreyas Iyer in a 66-run stand before adding a match-defining 94-run partnership with Tilak Varma.Kishan struck nine fours and two sixes during his 44-ball 81, bringing up his 13th T20 half-century in just 31 deliveries. Tilak provided the perfect finishing touch with an unbeaten 60 off only 29 balls as India surged to 219/5.Zimbabwe never threatened the target despite Brian Bennett's brisk 32. Debutant Yash Thakur impressed with 2/30, while Abhishek Sharma claimed 3/17. Prince Yadav struck twice before leaving the field with a hamstring injury.India eventually wrapped up a comprehensive 90-run victory to clinch the series with one match still to play.
Article Summary: India beat Zimbabwe by 90 runs to clinch T20 series 2-0. Ishan Kishan hits brilliant 81 off 44 deliveries to earn Player of the Match award. Wicketkeeper- batter misses run-out opportunity behind the stumps. KISHan later saw the funny side of the incident, joking about it.

NEW DELHI: Shreyas Iyer's first series triumph as India's T20I captain was built on a fearless brand of cricket, and the skipper believes the young side's ability to stay positive and attack every opportunity has been the biggest takeaway from their dominant campaign against Zimbabwe.India sealed an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series with a commanding 90-run victory in the second T20I on Saturday, but for Iyer, the result was more than just another win — it was a reflection of the team's aggressive mindset and belief in its young players.Batting first, India recovered from an early wobble to post a massive 219/5, powered by Ishan Kishan's brilliant 81 and Tilak Varma's unbeaten 60. Article Title: India crush Zimbabwe by 90 runs as Shreyas Iyer clinches first series win as captain
Article Text:
Tilak Varma, Ishan Kishan. (Photo/BCCI)

India sealed the three-match T20I series against Zimbabwe with a 90-run win in the second match on Saturday, taking an unassailable 2-0 lead.Half-centuries from Ishan Kishan and Tilak Varma, followed by a disciplined bowling effort, helped India outplay the hosts after posting 219/5.The victory also gave new T20I captain Shreyas Iyer his first series win after India lost the previous two T20I series under his leadership against Ireland (0-2) and England (0-4).Chasing 220, Zimbabwe's task became difficult after losing five wickets inside the first nine overs. They were eventually bowled out for 129.Brian Bennett gave Zimbabwe an aggressive start, scoring 32 off 19 balls with three fours and three sixes. He took on debutant Yash Thakur, hitting him for a six and a four in succession, but the pacer responded immediately as Bennett's attempted ramp shot was caught by wicketkeeper Kishan.Thakur finished with 2/30, while the Indian bowlers kept picking up wickets at regular intervals.Ryan Burl and Tadi Marumani made scores in the 20s, but Zimbabwe never managed to build a partnership that could put pressure on India.Part-time spinners Tilak Varma and Abhishek Sharma also chipped in with wickets, with Abhishek returning figures of 3/17 as India wrapped up the innings comfortably.India, however, suffered an injury concern when pacer Prince Yadav walked off the field holding his hamstring after bowling 1.2 overs.He finished with figures of 2/10.Earlier, India recovered from 29/2 after being asked to bat first.Kishan first added 66 runs for the third wicket with captain Shreyas Iyer, who scored 25, before putting together a 94-run stand with Tilak Varma.Kishan made 81 off 44 balls. He reached his fifty in 31 deliveries before adding another 31 runs in just 13 balls. Much of his scoring came on the leg side, where he repeatedly found the boundary.He hit Bennett for two fours through the mid-wicket region and later struck pacer Brad Evans for two fours and a six in the same area.Tilak remained unbeaten on 60 off 29 balls. He reached his fifty in just 23 deliveries and attacked Zimbabwe's leading pacer Blessing Muzarabani with three successive boundaries. One of those came with a late dab behind point using the bowler's pace, while he also hit Evans for a six over mid-wicket.India scored 61 runs in the final five overs.The visitors had earlier lost both openers cheaply.Abhishek Sharma was caught at point off Muzarabani, while Vaibhav Sooryavanshi made 20 off nine balls, including a sequence of 4, 6, 4 and 4 against Richard Ngarava. The left-arm pacer, however, had the final word as Sooryavanshi mistimed a bouncer to Muzarabani at mid-on.From there, Kishan and Tilak took control to set up another comfortable win for India.

Article Title: Tilak Varma overtakes MS Dhoni, Raina in India's T20I run-scoring list
Article Text:
Tilak Varma

India batter and T20I vice-captain Tilak Varma moved up the list of India's highest run-scorers in T20 internationals after his unbeaten half-century against Zimbabwe in the second T20I on Saturday.Tilak scored 60 not out from 29 balls, hitting five fours and three sixes at a strike rate of 206.90. The knock helped him go past MS Dhoni Suresh Raina and teammate Ishan Kishan to become India's seventh-highest run-scorer in T20Is.The left-hander has now scored 1,634 runs in 58 T20Is and 55 innings at an average of 44.16 and a strike rate of 145.37. His record includes two centuries and nine fifties, with a highest score of 120 not out.Tilak overtook Dhoni, who finished with 1,617 runs in 98 T20Is at an average of 37.60 and a strike rate of 126.13, with two fifties.He also moved ahead of Raina, who scored 1,605 runs in 78 matches at an average of 29.18 and a strike rate of 134.87, including one century and five fifties.India's leading run-scorers in T20Is remain Rohit Sharma (4,231 runs), Virat Kohli (4,188) and Suryakumar Yadav (3,272).Tilak has scored 451 runs in 18 T20I innings this year at an average of 34.69 and a strike rate of nearly 149. He has registered three fifties, with his unbeaten 60 against Zimbabwe now his highest score of the year.Earlier in the match, Zimbabwe won the toss and chose to field.India lost Abhishek Sharma for 8 and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi for 20 off nine balls, before Ishan Kishan and captain Shreyas Iyer added 66 runs for the third wicket.Iyer scored 25 from 20 balls with four boundaries before getting out. Kishan then shared a 94-run partnership with Tilak and finished with 81 off 44 balls, hitting nine fours and two sixes.India posted 219/5 in their 20 overs.For Zimbabwe, Blessing Muzarabani returned figures of 1/36 in four overs, while Newman Nyamhuri picked up 1/25 in three overs.
Article Summary: Tilak Varma scores unbeaten 60 against Zimbabwe in second T20I on Saturday. Left-hander moves past MS Dhoni and Ishan Kishan to become India's seventh- highest run-scorer in T20Is. He has scored 1,634 runs in 58 T20is and 55 innings at an average of 44.16.

Article Title: Tim David questions Pakistan bowler Usman Tariq's bowling action, gestures 'no-ball' after dismissal
Article Text:
Photo/screengrab

Australia batter Tim David became the latest batter to question Pakistan spinner Usman Tariq 's bowling action after being dismissed by him during a men's Hundred match on Friday.David, playing for Trent Rockets against Birmingham Phoenix, edged a full delivery outside off stump to the wicketkeeper. After the dismissal, he appeared to suggest to the umpire that the delivery should have been called a no-ball, seemingly because of Tariq's bowling action. David also instinctively signalled for a review before deciding against it. The umpire did not uphold the appeal, and David walked off.According to MCC Law 21.2, a delivery is fair if the ball is not thrown. The law states that once the bowler's arm reaches shoulder level during the delivery swing, the elbow must not be partially or completely straightened before the ball leaves the hand.The striker's-end umpire has the primary responsibility for judging whether a delivery is fair, although the bowler's-end umpire can also call a no-ball if they believe the ball has been thrown.David appeared to be indicating that Tariq's action did not comply with the law and should have resulted in a no-ball.Tariq's bowling action has remained under scrutiny for some time. During the 2024 Pakistan Super League, umpires Asif Yaqoob and Richard Illingworth reported him for a suspect bowling action to the match referee.His action was reported again by the on-field umpires during the 2025 PSL.Earlier this year, Australia all-rounder Cameron Green also appeared to question Tariq's action during the second T20I against Pakistan. After being dismissed by the spinner, Green mimicked a baseball-style throwing motion, referring to Tariq's bowling action.Despite the criticism on the field and the discussion around his action, Usman Tariq has been cleared by the International Cricket Council (ICC).
Article Summary: Tim David appeared to question Pakistan spinner Usman Tariq's bowling action after being dismissed by him during a men's Hundred match on Friday. David edged a full delivery outside off stump to the wicketkeeper. After the dismissal, he appeared to suggest to the umpire that the delivery should have been called a no-ball. The umpire did not uphold the appeal, and David walked off.

Article Title: India script history, equal world record for most 200-plus T20I totals in a calendar year

India's batting machine rewrites record books again

NEW DELHI: India continued their batting revolution in T20 Internationals on Saturday, matching their own world record for the most 200-plus totals in a calendar year after piling up 219/5 against Zimbabwe in the second T20I.The 219-run effort was India's ninth 200-plus total in T20Is in 2026, drawing level with the record they had set in 2024. No other full-member nation has managed more than six such totals in a single calendar year, underlining India's sustained dominance with the bat in the shortest format.More remarkably, India have now crossed the 200-run mark 52 times in T20Is, extending their all-time record. The next-best side, South Africa, has managed the feat only 29 times, highlighting the gulf between India and the rest of the cricketing world when it comes to consistently posting mammoth totals.India's remarkable consistency is reflected in the all-time list of most 200-plus totals in a calendar year.They first set the benchmark with nine such scores in 2024 and have now equalled it in 2026. India also produced seven 200-plus totals in 2023, meaning they occupy three of the top five spots on the list.The latest milestone came despite India stumbling to 29/2 after being asked to bat first.Zimbabwe struck twice inside the powerplay as Abhishek Sharma and the in-form Vaibhav Sooryavanshi departed cheaply.Abhishek offered a simple catch to Ryan Burl off Blessing Muzarabani, while Sooryavanshi, after racing to 20 off just nine deliveries with four boundaries and a six, miscued a Richard Ngarava bouncer to mid-on.With India under pressure, Ishan Kishan and skipper Shreyas Iyer steadied the innings through a composed 66-run partnership for the third wicket.Kishan then found an ideal ally in Tilak Varma as the pair added 94 runs to completely wrest control away from Zimbabwe.Kishan struck a superb 81, perfectly pacing his innings. He reached his half-century in 31 balls before accelerating spectacularly, smashing 31 more runs in just 13 deliveries. His leg-side strokeplay proved particularly destructive, with Zimbabwe's bowlers repeatedly punished through the mid-wicket region.Tilak complemented him brilliantly with an unbeaten 60 off just 29 balls, silencing recent discussions over his strike rate. The left-hander raced to his fifty in only 23 deliveries, mixing elegant placement with clean power hitting.The duo powered India to 61 runs in the final five overs, lifting the visitors to an imposing 219/5.Speaking during the innings break, Tilak credited Kishan for setting the tone."We felt anything around 200 would be a really good score here. But when you think about 200, obviously the score can go to 220, especially the way Ishan batted. It was tremendous to watch," Tilak said.The 23-year-old also revealed that conversations with head coaches Gautam Gambhir and VVS Laxman had prompted him to focus on scoring more through the ground rather than relying solely on aerial shots."I've been talking with Gautam sir and now with Laxman sir about finding the gaps. If you hit through the ground, your consistency improves. I worked really hard during the break after the England series, and I'm happy it came through today," he added.With another 200-plus total added to an ever-growing collection, India's batting unit continues to redefine T20I standards.
Article Summary: India match their own world record for the most 200-plus totals in a calendar year. They posted 219/5 against Zimbabwe in the second T20I on Saturday. India have now crossed the 200-run mark 52 times in T20Is, extending their all-time record.

Article Title: Who is Yash Thakur? Vidarbha pacer making his India debut in second T20I against Zimbabwe
Article Text:
Yash Thakur

Who is Yash Thakur?

Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza won the toss and elected to field against India in the second T20 International on Saturday, as the visitors handed a debut to Vidarbha fast bowler Yash Thakur Yash replaced Ashok Sharma in the playing XI. Ashok had made his T20I debut in the series opener on July 23 but went wicketless despite bowling his full quota of four overs.India lead the three-match series 1-0 after registering a seven-wicket win in the opening game.The 27-year-old fast bowler from Vidarbha earned his maiden India cap after consistent performances in domestic cricket and for India A.Before his international debut, Yash had played 74 T20 matches, taking 110 wickets in 74 innings.He has also featured in 22 Indian Premier League (IPL) matches for Lucknow Super Giants and Punjab Kings, claiming 27 wickets.Yash represented India A in the tri-series in Sri Lanka last month, where he picked up five wickets in three matches. He also played two unofficial Test matches against Sri Lanka A in Galle and took five wickets.The Vidarbha seamer has played 32 first-class matches, taking 93 wickets, and 57 List A games, where he has claimed 90 wickets.Since making his List A debut in 2017, Yash has established himself as one of Vidarbha's leading bowlers across formats. Along with nearly 100 wickets in 57 one-day matches, he has taken 110 wickets in 74 T20s and 27 wickets in 22 IPL appearances, including a five-wicket haul.Before joining Punjab Kings for IPL 2026, Yash made an impact in domestic cricket by finishing as Vidarbha's highest wicket-taker in both the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy and the Vijay Hazare Trophy.

Article Title: CWG 2026: Neeraj Chopra checks in after long injury rehab
Article Text:
Neeraj Chopra(Image credit: X)

India’s star attraction Neeraj Chopra finally touched down in Glasgow on Saturday morning ahead of a high-stakes men’s javelin throw competition.Sporting an all-black outfit comprising a sweatshirt, track pants and a black cap, Chopra cut a relaxed figure as he made his way into the hotel where the athletics and para-athletics contingent are staying. The Olympic and world champion returns to the CWG after missing the 2022 Birmingham edition because of injury.Gold Coast champion in 2018, Chopra enters Glasgow with just one competition under his belt over the last year. Since finishing a disappointing eighth at the World Championships in Tokyo last Sept while battling a troublesome lower back injury, the 28-year-old has stayed away from competition, focusing entirely on rehabilitation and recovery.His only appearance since then came in the Doha Diamond League, where an 85.69m throw fetched him fourth place.Having also dealt with ankle, shoulder, wrist and adductor issues in recent years, Chopra has taken a cautious approach to his return. “I’m coming from Switzerland. The preparations have been good. After the Doha DL, we increased the intensity of my workouts and fitness regime. It took time to recover from injury issues this time,” Chopra said after arriving in Glasgow.Neeraj will once again renew his rivalry with Pakistan’s Olympic and defending CWG champion Arshad Nadeem, while Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage, who produced a world-leading 92.62m in Rome DL earlier this month, enters the competition as the man in form. Pathirage had also finished ahead of Chopra in Doha. “The weather seems cloudy and rainy here. Hoping for weather to get somewhat warmer on my competition day,” Chopra said.Chopra will be joined by Rohit Yadav and Yash Vir Singh in the men’s javelin throw,. The qualifying is on July 30.
